{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 treated PDB 1acc chain A, anthrax protective antigen, as one whole-chain domain: d1acca_ (SUNID 43828), family f.11.1.1, superfamily f.11.1, fold f.11 (all named Anthrax protective antigen), in class f, Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides.

By SCOPe 2.08, this was replaced by two separately classified domains, using PDB residue numbering:
• d1acca2 (SUNID 238522), A:14–225: family PA14 (b.179.1.1), superfamily PA14-like (b.179.1), fold Anthrax protective antigen N-terminal-like (b.179), class b, All beta proteins.
• d1acca1 (SUNID 238521), A:226–735: family f.60.1.1, superfamily f.60.1, and fold f.60, all named Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like, remaining in class f.

This is a revision of the evolutionary units represented by the classification, not a biological change in the protein. The N-terminal PA14 module can be considered separately from the rest of the chain when tracing ancestry across different protein architectures. A polypeptide chain need not constitute one evolutionary domain, and SCOPe units need not coincide with every structural or functional subdivision described elsewhere. Family membership supports a closer evolutionary relationship; superfamily membership supports broader common ancestry. Shared fold or class alone does not establish homology. Conversely, the two different classifications do not by themselves prove that no deeper relationship could exist.

Homology searches should therefore use the two domain regions separately, with domain-specific sequences or profiles and local alignment coverage, while retaining the whole-chain architecture as context. A PA14-region match must not be interpreted as homology across the entire protective-antigen chain or as evidence of toxin function. Likewise, a template matching one module cannot automatically model the other module or their relative arrangement. Transfer of precise function requires additional functional evidence. Record the SCOPe release, SID, and residue boundaries, and remap legacy d1acca_ hits before comparing results across releases; the old single-domain record is not interchangeable with either replacement.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of SCOP hierarchy and domain-based homology inference","mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1acc","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2/parents"]}]}
